title: Form validation attributes
summary: Let the browser check input for you with required, minlength, min, max, pattern and placeholder.

quiz.q: Which attribute stops a form from being sent when a field is empty?
quiz.explain: `required` blocks an empty value. `minlength` only checks non-empty text, and `placeholder` is just a hint.

quiz.q: Limit the number to at most 100.
quiz.explain: `max` sets the largest allowed number. `maxlength` is for the number of characters in text.
`[0-9]` means one digit and `{4}` means four of them, so the full value must be exactly four digits.

quiz.q: Why must a server still validate data even if the HTML has validation attributes?
quiz.explain: A visitor can edit the page or send a request without a browser. Only checks on the server can be trusted.

exercise.task:
Add validation attributes to the sign-up form in `index.html`.

- `#username`: required, with `minlength="3"`.
- `#email`: required, with a `placeholder`.
- `#age`: `type="number"`, `min="18"`, `max="60"`.
- `#pin`: a `pattern` that allows exactly four digits, e.g. `[0-9]{4}`, and `required`.
hints: The inputs already exist with ids. Add attributes to their opening tags, not new elements.
required stands alone. minlength, min, max, pattern and placeholder each need ="value".

<input id="username" name="username" type="text" required minlength="3">
<input id="email" name="email" type="email" required placeholder="you@example.com">
<input id="age" name="age" type="number" min="18" max="60">
<input id="pin" name="pin" type="text" required pattern="[0-9]{4}">

checks.name: #email is required and has a placeholder
#pin is required and has a four-digit pattern
